title: Historic Visit: Kisumu Governor Peter Anyang’ Nyong’o Arrives in Acholi Land to Rekindle Deep Cultural Ties
description:
Gulu City — Kenya’s Kisumu County Governor, Prof. Peter Anyang’ Nyong’o, is currently in Acholi land, Northern Uganda, on a landmark cultural and heritage visit aimed at strengthening long-standing historical ties between the Acholi people and Luo-speaking communities of Kenya. The governor arrived earlier this week accompanied by his wife, Mama Dorothy Nyong’o, and members of his delegation, and has since begun a series of engagements across the sub-region.

The visit is anchored in shared ancestry, language, and cultural traditions linking the Acholi of Northern Uganda and the Luo of Kenya. Cultural leaders and organisers describe the trip as a form of people-to-people diplomacy, focusing on cultural preservation, inter-generational knowledge transfer, and renewed regional cooperation that goes beyond formal state relations.

Since his arrival, Prof. Nyong’o has been received in Gulu City, which serves as the central hub for most of his engagements. His itinerary includes visits to Madi-Opei, Pawidi, and surrounding areas within the Acholi sub-region, where he is expected to tour historical and cultural sites linked to Luo heritage and Acholi identity. He is also scheduled to engage with cultural institutions and community organisations, including meetings at the TASK Centre in Gulu, a key venue for Acholi cultural dialogue.

The visit has been organised and supported by prominent Acholi and regional figures, including Ambassador Dr. Olara Otunnu, a former United Nations Under-Secretary-General, who has played a central role in coordinating the cultural engagement. Other notable personalities expected to interact with the Kenyan governor include Chief Justice Alfonse Owiny-Dollo, a respected son of Acholi and one of the region’s most senior national leaders, as well as senior cultural leaders, elders, and intellectuals such as Komakech and other custodians of Acholi heritage.

Organisers say the visit is also intended to inspire young people in Acholi land to reconnect with their cultural roots while exploring opportunities for cross-border collaboration in education, culture, and local economic development, particularly in agriculture, trade, and cultural tourism. Kisumu’s position as a regional economic hub on Lake Victoria has been cited as a potential bridge for future cooperation between western Kenya and Northern Uganda.

The current visit draws strong historical parallels to an earlier journey made by Jaramogi Oginga Odinga, Kenya’s renowned nationalist leader, who travelled to Acholi land in 1954. That historic visit is remembered for strengthening cultural consciousness and unity among Luo-speaking communities across colonial borders, and many cultural leaders say Prof. Nyong’o’s presence echoes that legacy decades later.

Cultural custodians in Acholi have welcomed the visit as a revival of shared history and identity, noting that it reinforces unity, mutual respect, and cultural pride across generations. Leaders have expressed optimism that the engagement will lead to sustained exchanges between Acholi and Kisumu institutions, including cultural documentation, heritage education, and people-centred development initiatives.

Governor Nyong’o is expected to continue his engagements in Acholi land over the coming days, meeting elders, cultural scholars, youth leaders, and regional dignitaries before concluding his visit.

Kyoga TV will continue to provide updates and exclusive coverage as this historic visit unfolds.
author: Kyoga TV News Desk

title: Police Investigate Alleged Assault on Bobi Wine and Supporters During Gulu Campaign
description:
Ugandan police have launched investigations into allegations that security officers assaulted opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, and several of his supporters during a campaign event in Gulu City, northern Uganda, over the weekend. One person has since been reported dead following the incident.

The incident occurred as Bobi Wine, leader of the National Unity Platform (NUP), was mobilizing supporters ahead of the January 2026 general elections. According to NUP officials, security personnel blocked the opposition convoy, disrupted the rally, and allegedly beat Kyagulanyi and members of his team. Several supporters were reportedly injured, with some receiving treatment at health facilities in Gulu.

Bobi Wine later shared photos and videos on social media showing injuries and scenes of chaos, accusing security forces of using excessive force to block his campaign activities. He said the violence was unprovoked and called on authorities to respect democratic freedoms during the election period.

Following the clashes, reports emerged that a teenage student later died after sustaining injuries during the unrest. Opposition officials have linked the death to the campaign violence, while police say investigations are ongoing to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the fatality.

The Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) and police have disputed the opposition’s account, stating that Bobi Wine had violated campaign guidelines by organizing an illegal procession and moving outside approved routes. Security agencies maintain that their intervention was intended to restore order and enforce electoral regulations.

In response to public concern, the Uganda Police Force confirmed that it is investigating both the alleged assault on opposition supporters and the reported death. Police spokespersons said disciplinary action would be taken if any officers are found to have acted unlawfully.

The incident has drawn criticism from opposition figures and civil society groups, who say it highlights shrinking political space and growing intolerance toward opposition activities, particularly in northern Uganda. The Electoral Commission has urged all political actors and security agencies to exercise restraint and comply with the law to ensure peaceful campaigns.

The Gulu clash comes amid heightened political activity nationwide, as candidates intensify campaigns, raising renewed debate about security conduct, political freedoms, and the integrity of Uganda’s electoral process.
author: Kyoga TV News Desk

title: Uganda Concludes Two-Day Presidential Nominations: Eight Men Cleared, No Women on the Ballot
description:
Kampala, Uganda — Kyoga TV News Desk
The Electoral Commission has completed its two-day presidential nomination exercise, officially confirming eight candidates who will appear on the ballot in the January 2026 general election. The process, which ran from September 23 to 24 at the Commission’s headquarters in Lweza–Lubowa, Wakiso District, ended without a single female candidate being cleared — the first such scenario in nearly two decades.

Incumbent President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni of the National Resistance Movement was nominated on the first day and pledged continuity, saying his campaign will focus on economic transformation, infrastructure, healthcare, and fighting corruption. He thanked his party for the overwhelming support and urged Ugandans to trust the NRM’s record in delivering stability and growth.

On the second day, opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, of the National Unity Platform, was cleared to run. Addressing his supporters, he described his candidacy as a mission to liberate the country from dictatorship. He called on President Museveni to allow a peaceful transition, assuring Ugandans that his struggle is about freedom, justice, and dignity.

Maj. Gen. (Rtd.) Gregory Mugisha Muntu Oyera of the Alliance for National Transformation, who submitted additional signatures shortly before the deadline, used his post-nomination briefing to highlight the importance of accountability and justice. He warned that peace without justice is fragile and promised to lead a government that respects both.

Nathan Nandala Mafabi of the Forum for Democratic Change presented himself as the candidate of reform, vowing to overhaul Uganda’s health system and end the elite’s reliance on foreign medical treatment. He pledged to restore integrity in governance and provide services that meet the needs of ordinary citizens.

Mubarak Sserunga Munyagwa of the Common Man’s Party said his campaign would prioritise economic fairness and empower the ordinary Ugandan. He promised quick action on cost-of-living issues and unveiled a plan to place the common man at the centre of government policy.

Robert Kasibante of the National Peasants Party emphasised agriculture, food security, and rural development, promising policies that directly benefit farming communities.

Elton Joseph Mabirizi of the Conservative Party, who briefly faced a technical hitch before clearance, pledged reconciliation and inclusivity, saying his government would ensure that all Ugandans feel part of the nation’s progress.

Frank Bulira Kabinga of the Revolutionary People’s Party said federal restructuring was his top priority and assured his supporters that his campaign would deliver a “gigantic surprise” at the ballot box.

While these eight men successfully navigated the rigorous process, dozens of other aspirants were turned away. Some failed to collect the required minimum of 9,800 verified signatures from at least 98 districts, while others submitted forms with errors such as invalid national IDs or nominators outside eligible constituencies. Well-known hopefuls including John Katumba, Joseph Kabuleta, Willy Mayambala, and Nancy Kalembe did not make it to the ballot. Their failure has been attributed to incomplete paperwork, late submissions, or insufficient endorsements.

The Electoral Commission has set September 29 as the official start of campaigns, with Ugandans scheduled to cast their votes on January 12, 2026. The eight-way race, dominated by the face-off between Museveni and Bobi Wine, is expected to test Uganda’s democratic institutions and determine the political direction of the country.

Kyoga TV News Desk will continue to provide updates as campaigns unfold across the nation.
author: Kyoga TV News Desk

title: UPC Barred from Fielding Presidential Candidate in 2026 Elections Amid Leadership Crisis
description:
The Uganda People's Congress (UPC), one of Uganda’s oldest and most influential political parties, has been disqualified from fielding a presidential candidate in the 2026 general elections. The Electoral Commission (EC) cited ongoing internal disputes, breaches of the party constitution, and binding court rulings as the primary reasons for the unprecedented decision.

At the center of the controversy is Jimmy James Michael Akena, the current party president. A High Court ruling in Miscellaneous Cause No. 148 of 2025 determined that Akena had already served the maximum two terms permitted under the UPC constitution. Despite attempts by the party to extend his tenure through a virtual extraordinary delegates’ conference, the EC declared these actions unconstitutional and invalid.

The disqualification also affected other senior UPC figures. Denis Enap Adim failed to meet the constitutional requirements for nomination, while Peter Walubiri Mukidi was excluded for not participating in the official nomination process. The situation has deepened a leadership crisis that has left the party fragmented and facing uncertainty ahead of the elections.

Social media platforms have been rife with speculation and false reports, including claims that Akena had been cleared to contest. These claims were swiftly refuted by legal representatives within the UPC, emphasizing that no nominations had been officially approved by the EC.

Founded in 1960, the UPC has a long and storied history in Uganda’s political landscape. The party played a leading role in the country’s transition to independence in 1962 under Milton Obote and the alliance with the Kabaka Yekka party. Over the decades, the UPC has experienced periods of both prominence and marginalization, but it has remained a symbol of Uganda’s post-independence political evolution.

Political analysts warn that the party’s absence from the 2026 presidential race could significantly reshape the electoral landscape. With opposition parties and new political movements gaining traction, UPC’s disqualification may alter voter alignments and influence coalition dynamics.

Party insiders admit that resolving the internal disputes and restoring cohesion will be a monumental challenge. With the nomination deadline approaching, UPC is confronted with the stark reality of potentially missing the presidential race for the first time in its history. Observers say this moment represents both a critical test for the party and a reflection of the broader challenges facing established political organizations in Uganda today.
author: Kyoga TV

title: Premier League Weekend Roundup: Drama at Old Trafford, Late Arsenal Rescue, and Villa’s Woes Continue
description:
Red cards, late drama and missed chances defined another gripping weekend in the Premier League.

From Manchester United’s chaotic victory over Chelsea to Arsenal’s stoppage-time equaliser against Manchester City, fans were treated to a round of football that underlined just how unpredictable the season is shaping up to be.

At Old Trafford, Manchester United breathed life into their stuttering campaign with a 2-1 victory over Chelsea. The match was turned on its head inside the first five minutes when Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sánchez was sent off for a reckless foul. United seized the advantage, with Bruno Fernandes marking his 100th goal for the club before Casemiro doubled the lead. The Brazilian midfielder’s afternoon ended early too, dismissed before half-time to even the numbers. Chelsea’s Trevoh Chalobah struck late to set up a nervy finish, but Erik ten Hag’s side held firm to secure three vital points.

The weekend’s showpiece clash at the Emirates did not disappoint. Manchester City looked on course for victory after Erling Haaland’s early strike, but Arsenal grew into the contest, pressing relentlessly in search of an equaliser. Their persistence was rewarded deep into stoppage time, when Gabriel Martinelli latched onto a clever pass from Eberechi Eze to rescue a 1-1 draw. The result keeps both sides firmly in the title conversation, though City may rue letting two points slip so late.

Aston Villa’s wait for a first league win of the season continued, despite facing ten-man Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. Matty Cash gave Unai Emery’s side a rare lead, only for Wilson Isidor to equalise after Sunderland’s Reinildo had been shown red. Emery did not mince words afterwards, branding his side’s performance “lazy” as pressure mounts on Villa to turn their season around.

Nottingham Forest’s Ange Postecoglou remains without a Premier League win, though he insists progress is being made. Forest took the lead through Neco Williams against Burnley but were pegged back as the match finished 1-1. It is the third straight game without victory for Forest under the Australian coach, whose attacking philosophy has yet to translate into results.

Across the league, fine margins defined the weekend’s drama: United clinging on with ten men, Arsenal’s stoppage-time lifeline, Villa’s inability to punish a weakened Sunderland, and Forest’s missed chances for a breakthrough win. With the table beginning to take shape, every point feels crucial, and this weekend showed again why the Premier League remains the most unpredictable competition in world football.

Weekend Results at a Glance
- Manchester United 2–1 Chelsea
- Arsenal 1–1 Manchester City
- Sunderland 1–1 Aston Villa
- Nottingham Forest 1–1 Burnley
author: Olica Felix
